async-route-errors.why: In Express 4 a rejected promise in an async handler is not forwarded to the error middleware, so the request hangs.
async-route-errors.fix: Wrap the body in try/catch and call `next(err)`, or use an async wrapper. Express 5 handles this itself.

avoid-print.why: `print` output is unstructured and cannot be filtered or turned off in release builds.

eqeqeq.why: `==` converts types before comparing (`0 == ''` is true), which hides bugs. Comparing to `null` with `== null` is the one accepted idiom and is not reported.

no-assertionless-tests.why: A test with no assertion passes unless the code throws, so it cannot catch a wrong result.
no-assertionless-tests.fix: Assert on the result. If a helper asserts for you, this is a false positive: suppress it with a reason.

no-async-foreach.why: `forEach` ignores the promises an `async` callback returns, so the loop ends before the work does and failures become unhandled rejections.
no-async-foreach.fix: Use `for...of` with `await` for sequential work, or `await Promise.all(items.map(...))` for concurrent work.

no-atom-from-input.why: Atoms are never garbage collected; creating them from input lets a caller exhaust the atom table and crash the node.
no-atom-from-input.fix: Use `String.to_existing_atom/1`, or keep the value a string.

no-dangerously-set-inner-html.why: `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` renders a string as HTML, so untrusted text becomes a script-injection hole.
no-dangerously-set-inner-html.fix: Render the value as text, or sanitize it with a vetted library first.

no-empty-tests.why: An empty test always passes, so it counts as coverage while verifying nothing.
no-empty-tests.fix: Write the assertions, or mark it `it.todo` so the gap stays visible.

no-error-leak.why: Stack traces and raw messages show paths, versions and queries to whoever triggers the error.
no-error-leak.fix: Log the error on the server and send a generic message.

no-eval.why: `eval` runs a string as code, so anything that reaches it can run arbitrary code in your process.
no-eval.fix: Parse data with `JSON.parse`, and call functions directly instead of building code from strings.

no-explicit-any.why: `any` switches off type checking for everything it touches, so a wrong value type-checks and fails at runtime.
no-explicit-any.fix: Type the value, or use `unknown` and narrow it before use.

no-extend-native.why: Changing a built-in prototype affects every library in the process, and can break them or be broken by them.
no-extend-native.fix: Write a standalone helper function instead of adding to the prototype.

no-fatal-error.why: `fatalError` ends the app with no chance to recover; a shipped path should fail in a way the caller can handle.
no-fatal-error.fix: Throw or return an error and let the caller decide.

no-focused-tests.why: A focused test (`.only`, `fit`) makes the runner skip every other test, so CI stays green while the rest of the suite stops running.

no-hardcoded-secrets.why: A secret in source code is in every clone, every fork, and the git history forever.
no-hardcoded-secrets.fix: Read it from the environment or a secret manager, and rotate the exposed value.

no-implied-eval.why: `new Function(...)` and string timers compile a string into code, with the same risk as `eval`.
no-implied-eval.fix: Pass a function, not a string.

no-open-cors.why: Allowing every origin lets any website call the API from a visitor's browser, with their cookies if credentials are on.

no-panic.why: `panic` aborts the current goroutine or thread; a library that panics takes its caller down with it.
no-panic.fix: Return an error and let the caller decide.

no-permit-all.why: `permit!` accepts every parameter, so a caller can set fields it should not reach (mass assignment, CWE-915).
no-permit-all.fix: List the parameters the action accepts.

no-print-stack-trace.why: A stack trace printed to the console skips the logger, so it has no level, no context and may reach users.
no-print-stack-trace.fix: Pass the exception to the project's logger.

no-raw-markup.why: Marking text as safe markup turns off escaping; if any part of it came from a user, it is script injection (CWE-79).
no-raw-markup.fix: Let the template escape it, or sanitize it first.

no-shell-interpolation.why: `exec` runs the string in a shell, so a value containing `;` or `$(...)` runs as a command.
no-shell-interpolation.fix: Use `execFile` or `spawn` with an argument array so no shell reads the values.

no-unbounded-c-string.why: These functions write without knowing the size of the destination, so long input overruns the buffer (CWE-120).
no-unbounded-c-string.fix: Use a function that takes the size, or std::string.

no-unsafe-blocks.why: `unsafe` turns off the compiler's memory-safety guarantees for that block.
no-unsafe-blocks.fix: Check whether safe code can do the same; if not, document the invariant the block relies on.
no-unsafe-blocks.after:
// SAFETY: `ptr` is valid and uniquely borrowed for this write.
unsafe { *ptr = value; }

no-unsafe-deserialization.why: Deserializing bytes from an untrusted source can run code chosen by whoever wrote them (CWE-502).
no-unsafe-deserialization.fix: Read a data-only format such as JSON, or check the source before loading.

no-unwrap-expect.why: `unwrap()` and `expect()` panic on `None` or `Err`, taking the whole thread down.
no-unwrap-expect.fix: Propagate the error with `?`, or handle the failure case.

no-var.why: `var` is function-scoped and hoisted, so a variable can be read before it is assigned or leak out of its block.
no-var.fix: Use `const`, or `let` if the value is reassigned.

no-weak-hash.why: MD5, SHA-1 and DES are broken for security uses: collisions are cheap to produce (CWE-327).
no-weak-hash.fix: Use SHA-256 or stronger; for passwords use a password hash.

prefer-object-spread.why: `Object.assign({}, a)` is the long way to copy an object.

prefer-template-literals.why: Building strings with `+` gets hard to read and easy to break as it grows.

strict-null-checks.why: A non-null assertion (`!`) tells the compiler a value cannot be null without checking, and crashes when it is.
strict-null-checks.fix: Handle the null case, or use optional chaining with a fallback.

use-v-html-carefully.why: `v-html` renders a string as HTML, so untrusted text becomes a script-injection hole.
use-v-html-carefully.fix: Render the value as text with `{{ }}`, or sanitize it first.
